title: Haunted Bournemouth venue where staff saw ghost during £1.2m refurbishment
excerpt: The haunting history of Bournemouth’s O2 Academy, formerly Boscombe Opera House, as staff report ghostly sightings during its 2006 refurbishment.
content:
Whether you're a die-hard sceptic or firmly believe things go bump in the night, many believe in a secret whispered in the shadows of one of Bournemouth’s most legendary entertainment venues.

Two decades ago, the heavy thud of sledgehammers and the whine of power tools echoed through the cavernous halls of Boscombe’s Opera House, now known to thousands of gig-goers as the O2 Academy.

The ambitious £1.2 million refurbishment was meant to simply strip back the tired decor of the former nightclub and breathe new life into the English Heritage-listed building.

Instead, it seemingly woke something up.

Staff who thought they were alone soon found themselves sharing the space with restless residents.

(Image: Echo)

In the autumn of 2006, just as the extensive revamp was getting under way, a string of inexplicable sightings and eerie noises sent shivers down the spines of the workers tasked with bringing the venue into the 21st century.

One terrified member of staff recounted a chilling encounter in Benedict’s bar.

They were standing alone when a sudden noise prompted them to turn around.

Glancing into a mirror, they saw the reflection of a figure standing against the far wall.

The sudden shock was enough to make them flee the room immediately, utterly convinced that there was something fundamentally unsettling lurking within the walls.

Cleaner Tony Lundberg, who at the time had already dedicated two decades of his life to working at the Opera House, knew exactly what they meant.

He was absolutely convinced that the grand old building was haunted by the ghost of a young woman, adding to a supernatural tapestry woven throughout the venue's labyrinthine corridors and hidden staircases.

Paranormal investigators called in during the height of the renovations even managed to photograph a strange red light that appeared to illuminate a figure draped in cloth, suggesting the building was so steeped in past lives that it was almost destined to be haunted.

Perhaps it is little wonder the spirits felt disturbed by the sudden intrusion of builders.

(Image: Newsquest)

The bricks and mortar of this magnificent building hold more than a century of memories.

Over the decades, it has lived multiple lives as a town hall, a cinema, a casino, and a grand theatre.

Its stage has been graced by legends.

In the 1960s, the venue vibrated to the sounds of Pink Floyd, Status Quo, Led Zeppelin, Thin Lizzy, and David Bowie.

In the 1980s, the dark, atmospheric chords of The Sisters of Mercy and the pop anthems of Frankie Goes to Hollywood filled the air.

Today, as the O2 Academy Bournemouth, the venue continues to draw massive crowds, pulsating with the energy of modern performers and ecstatic fans.

Yet, when the stage lights fade, the crowds disperse, and the final chords ring out into the night, one has to wonder if the phantoms of the Opera House step back out from the shadows.

As we look back exactly twenty years after those chilling encounters were first reported, the question remains whether the ghosts have finally found peace, or if they still watch silently from the upper balconies.

Have you ever experienced anything paranormal or unexplainable while working at or visiting the venue, either in its Opera House days or as the O2 Academy?

We would love to hear your stories and build a definitive archive of Boscombe’s resident ghosts.
